about: The vegetable field, as /en/studio is one studio: grow every vegetable the galley needs to feed the farm's guests (founder, 2026-10-28). The field is sized to a FULL HOUSE every day of the year, so the galley never buys a vegetable; on an average night the surplus is sold. scripts/site/farming.mjs reads this file and src/components/site/site.json (zone `veg`) and writes public/designs/farming/data/. The 2D (farming-plan.tsx) and the 3D (scripts/site/render/farming.html) both read the generated plan. Facts and sources follow guide/grow/vegetables.md; [V] verified, [E] estimated, [A] assumed.

people.about: Who eats from the galley on a full house: 2 guests in each of the 2 studios, 3 en-suite rooms and 6 tents (guide/business/model.md), plus the team of about 7 who eat one meal a day there [A]. Events cook for their own numbers and buy what the field can't give.
people.averageNote: about 2,700 guest-days a year in the base case (guide/business/model.md)

menu.about: Grams of each vegetable on a guest's plate in a day, breakfast and dinner together [A], about 510 g with potato and chilli (D-052): a little over the WHO's 400 g of fruit and vegetables, because the galley cooks most of it.

bed.about: Beds as the guide lays them: 1.2 m wide, 10 m long, raised 20 cm; 0.5 m paths between beds, 1 m paths between blocks of 10 beds and round the field.
bed.lossNote: a quarter more beds than the plate needs, for pests, a failed planting and the rain season's losses [A]

start.about: The field starts with the two rows of blocks nearest the gate (founder, 2026-10-29; D-050): 6 blocks of 10 beds, 60 beds. A full house every day needs more; the start covers an average week with room to spare and the galley buys the rest on the busiest weeks. Each crop keeps its share of the beds. The other two rows are added when the bookings show the need, on the same layout.

season.about: Weeks a year a bed can grow: about 46, leaving 6 weeks to rest, compost and rebuild it [A]. Season C (July to September) is drip only, planted to the water the borehole proves.

crops.name: Tomato
crops.yieldNote: 20 t/ha on drip with stakes [E]; the national field average is about 8 t/ha [V CRP-17]
crops.watch: Tuta absoluta, late blight, bacterial wilt

crops.name: Sweet pepper
crops.yieldNote: 20 t/ha [E]; about 40 t/ha in the best open fields [V CRP-68]

crops.name: Eggplant
crops.yieldNote: 10 to 12 kg per 10 m row [V CRP-70]

crops.name: Amaranth (dodo)
crops.yieldNote: up to 10 t/ha of leaves per cutting round [V CRP-71]; 15 t/ha over six weekly cuts [E]

crops.name: Kale (sukuma)
crops.yieldNote: about 15 t/acre picked leaf by leaf [V CRP-69]

crops.name: Cucumber
crops.yieldNote: on a trellis 25 t/ha [E]; 8 to 10 kg per 10 m row on the ground [V CRP-70]

crops.name: Potato
crops.yieldNote: 15 t/ha [A AS-26], a placeholder: no Rwandan potato yield in the registers. Potato does best in the cool highlands; at the site's lower, warmer altitude expect less and more blight [U]
crops.watch: late blight, bacterial wilt, tuber moth

crops.name: Chilli
crops.yieldNote: 10 t/ha fresh [A AS-27], a placeholder: no Rwandan chilli yield in the registers; for the kitchen, not for sale (chilli for sale needs a written buyer [CRP-26])

nursery.about: A shade-net house for the seedlings, in the yard strip with the compost, tanks and tools, 33 m from the field (D-050): 8 x 4 m, 2.4 m high, 50 % net over a frame of eucalyptus poles every 2 m, trays on benches [A]. Inside (D-051, sizes [A]): two benches 7 m long and 1.2 m deep along the long sides, waist high, each holding 48 standard seedling trays (54 x 28 cm), with a 1.2 m path between them; the door at the end toward the field; a tap and a hose by the door.

fence.about: A 1.5 m wire-mesh fence on timber posts at 3 m, round the beds, with one gate on the garden walk to the galley.

bom.about: What the field needs to start, priced in RWF. Placeholders until three quotes per line [A], except the guide's verified Bugesera prices. `per` scales a line: bed (each bed), m (fence metres), once.

lines.item: Soil test at RAB (10 spots, one mixed sample)
Compost or manure, about 250 kg per 100 m² of bed
Agricultural lime, only if the test asks (about 200 kg per 1,000 m²)
Labour to dig and raise the beds
Drip tape, 16 mm, two lines a bed
Supply and header pipe, 32 mm PE
Valve and fittings at each block
Disc filter, 1 inch, at the tank
Main pipe from the tank, 40 mm PE
Wire mesh, 1.5 m high
Treated timber posts
Gate onto the garden walk
Shade net, 50 %
Poles and wire for the shade house
Seedling trays, 128 cells
Benches for the trays
Seed for a year (Holland Greentech), all twelve crops
Stakes and string for tomatoes, trellis for cucumbers
Pheromone traps for Tuta absoluta
Hoes, rakes, forks, watering cans, wheelbarrows, knapsack sprayer, crates, a scale
Gardeners for the first three months

fruit.about: The fruit row along the field's back fence, outside it (founder, 2026-10-29; D-052): banana mats (cooking and dessert bananas) and the fruit trees the study chose for this climate, grafted avocado, mango and lemon, and papaya at garden scale (study/design/crop-plan.md). For the galley's table and the guests, not for sale (banana and papaya are not cash lines there). Passion fruit and tree tomato stay out: virus in nearby fields, and too warm [CRP-33, CRP-34]. Spacing 3 m, counts [A AS-28].

banana.name: Banana
banana.note: a mat of 3 stems; cooking (matoke) and dessert bananas
